articles.title: State of CSS 2025
articles.description: The annual CSS survey returns, and the results should prove particularly interesting this year, if only to see the adoption and usage levels of all the new features and tools we’ve now got at our disposal. Worth filling out — tell ‘em we sent you. :)
articles.author: Devographics

articles.title: Partial Keyframes
articles.description: Josh shares a neat trick for creating dynamic, composable keyframe animations, explaining it clearly, and highlighting what we can do with it in his typical accessible style.
articles.author: Josh W. Comeau

articles.title: Exploring the CSS contrast-color() Function… A Second Time
articles.description: Thoughts on this evolved web accessibility function, highlighting its current limitations, potential future improvements, and alternative approaches.
articles.author: Daniel Schwarz

articles.title: Scroll-Driven Letter Grid
articles.description: Limited browser support for scroll-timeline means Safari and Firefox get left out of the fun here, but this is a neat technique, making use of variable fonts that change as you scroll.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: ▶  Jen Simmons on Declarative Web Push, Form Control Styling, & More
articles.description: Jen, from the WebKit team, joins Dave Rupert and Chris Coyier for a chat on various new CSS and Safari features like Form Control Styling, Declarative Web Push, Typography, contrast-color(), and more. There’s a video version too if you’d rather watch along.
articles.author: Shop Talk Show podcast

articles.title: Decoding the SVG path Element
articles.description: Aims to teach you the basics of <path> and its sometimes mystifying commands, there’s handy examples and visualizations too.
articles.author: Myriam Frisano

articles.title: 📄 Printing the Web: Making Webpages Look Good on Paper
articles.description: This is one of those things that’s probably low on your list of priorities, but Declan shares why we should bother, and how to go about it with CSS to create “clean, sleek, readable” documents.
articles.author: Declan Chidlow

articles.title: SF Symbols 7
articles.description: Currently in beta but available to download, Apple’s own library of icons has been updated and features hundreds of new symbols, with the total now closing in on 7,000 glyphs.
articles.author: Apple

articles.title: Astro 5.9 Released
articles.description: Adds experimental support for the highly requested Content Security Policy, along with a new helper function for rendering Markdown, logging changes, and more.
articles.author: Stoppa & Kane

articles.title: Storybook 9: The UI Component Workshop
articles.description: The popular one-stop tool for working on, and testing, frontend UI components gets a big update in terms of testing. Storybook Test offers interaction, visual, and accessibility testing, complete with a ‘watch mode’ for testing whenever you save, whether you’re working with React, Svelte, Next.js, React Native, and more.
articles.author: Michael Shilman

articles.title: Spectral.js: A More 'Paint-Like' Color Mixing Library
articles.description: If you have two colors to transition between, just tweening the RGB values can result in some rather ugly intermediate colors. Spectral.js uses Kubelka–Munk theory which more closely matches how paints work for a more visually satisfying result.
articles.author: Ronald van Wijnen

articles.title: Smooothy: A Smooth, Extensible Slider/Carousel Component
articles.description: Try out some demos here, which include customizations for keyboard control, parallax, speed, and there are implementations for React and Vue.
articles.author: Federico Valla
